category: hosted macOS CI runners and virtual machines

free_tier.stated: $0 per month, including 100 compute minutes per month and up to 1 concurrent virtual machine.
free_tier.notes: The pricing page states no credit card requirement. Compute minutes are consumed as base minutes multiplied by the machine-type multiplier: Mac M4 Base is 1x, Mac M4 Pro is 2x, and Mac M4 Max is 4x.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a running macOS virtual machine, not a stored object

retention.stated: Virtual machines are ephemeral: when a VM is terminated, deleted or expires its disk image and all data written to it are deleted from the host and are not retained; a CI runner is destroyed when its job completes.
retention.notes: A manually created instance is deleted after 60 minutes; a CI job can run for up to 6 hours.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page, homepage and terms read state no outbound data allowance or price; the API, dashboard and website are served over TLS.

interface_detail: A REST API manages VMs, a built-in remote terminal and remote display are in the dashboard, and direct native SSH reaches a VM; GitHub Actions and GitLab CI use the getmac runner label. Golang and Python SDKs are offered.
endpoint: unverified: no API endpoint URL is stated on the pages read
tooling: GitHub App installation and runs-on: getmac in workflows, GitLab CI executor, REST API, Golang and Python SDKs, SSH client and dashboard terminal; the user installs the repo integration.
chaining: A macOS CI job fits an existing GitHub Actions or GitLab pipeline; because a runner is destroyed with its data at job end, build artifacts must go to a separate storage record.

limits.value: 100 compute minutes per month on the Free plan; usage = base minutes x machine-type multiplier (1x M4 Base, 2x M4 Pro, 4x M4 Max)
up to 1 concurrent virtual machine on the Free plan
a CI job can run for up to 6 hours; a manually created instance is deleted after 60 minutes

limits_note: Free trials and proofs of concept may be modified, suspended or discontinued without notice; self-service plans carry no specific availability commitment.
binding_note: The 100 included compute minutes are consumed before the single concurrent VM slot becomes the obstruction on occasional builds.

identity_cost.detail: The dashboard sign-in page offers OAuth sign-in methods and links to the terms; the homepage states no credit card is required. Connecting a GitHub repository requires installing the GetMac GitHub App and logging in to GitHub. An email address is used for service notices under the terms.

reliability_note: CI runners are single-use and destroyed at job end; VMs are ephemeral with no backup, self-service plans have no availability commitment, and free trials may be withdrawn without notice.
confidence_note: Free-plan minutes and concurrency, the multiplier rule, sign-in gate, retention and job limits are quoted from GetMac's own pricing, homepage, terms and documentation read on 2026-11-24.

notes: Hosted macOS runners on Apple Silicon in a Lithuania data centre, with a USD 0 plan that includes 100 compute minutes a month and one concurrent VM. The 100 minutes are a standing monthly allowance, unlike a one-time trial. Paid tiers run from USD 11.99 a month. The sign-in methods shown on the dashboard page were not named in the captured text, so the exact identity gate beyond an email-based account is unverified; no card is stated as required.
